# Opposite-edge bars with sparse markers: unresolved task 3fd77db8

## Recurrence update (2026-09)
This task id was revisited with a 21x27 test (bg8; left edge color9 rows4-11, right edge color9 rows13-20; sparse color3 at (4,17),(6,21),(7,2),(9,22),(10,5),(11,17)). Eight demos were requested and eight test submissions failed; do not reuse any candidate construction from these tries. The correct rule is still unresolved.

Demos 1-8 show a consistent but not yet decoded operation: edge bars provide reference/boundaries, sparse marker cells are changed from marker color to 4, and additional fills use the marker color in geometry related to those points and boundary segments. Examples include rectangular color fills, rays/strips, and marker-connected expansions. Crucially, fill orientation/extent varies considerably; broad uniform fills of all marker rows, full left/right rays, or large rectangles on test all failed.

Failed test hypotheses/submissions on this recurrence: (1) change only marker points to 4; (2) fill broad left-side columns with marker color; (3) fill left-side blocks/rows; (4) fill nearly the whole area in marker color while preserving bars. All received incorrect feedback. The test target has 8 rows of the left-edge bar and 8 rows of the right-edge bar, with six sparse 3 points distributed through rows 4-11, suggesting edge-segment lengths and point configuration matter, but exact mechanism remains unknown. Since demo cap was exhausted without deriving it, do not claim a solved recipe; future recurrence should analyze all exact demo edits and, if allowed, use demos strategically before submitting.

## Observed task family
Eight demo pairs from Continual-ARC task `task-3fd77db8` showed two same-color boundary segments on opposite edges, a uniform field, and sparse markers of a second color. All eight submissions on its original test (22x6, bg9, color1 segments at right rows5–10 and left rows16–21, one color8 marker at (5,2)) were wrong. Do not reuse guessed test outputs. The consistent learned construction from demos: transform marker points into 4, then draw horizontal rays/fills in the marker color (or a related palette color) from each marker toward the opposite side, but exact direction/color depends on the boundary bars and marker patterns; also extend/fill regions associated with the boundary segments. This is unresolved and any recurrence merits fresh coordinate analysis.

## Solved recurrence: task-4547bc2a (2026-09)

Additional confirmed variant from a fresh episode: input 22x26, background 0, one full-width horizontal color-6 bar at row 1, and a partial color-6 bar at row 10 covering columns 0–20. Output retains the original dimensions. The corresponding demo had bg8, a full-width bar at row 3, and a partial bar at row 12; it filled the rest of the partial row with 1. This confirms the pattern: extend the partial horizontal stripe to full width using color 1 when the paired stripe establishes the horizontal full-bar context.


A new simple instance clarifies a reliable special case: background 7, full-width color-2 horizontal bar at row 3, and a second color-2 bar at row 12 ending at column 10 (cols 0–10), leaving cols 11–15 as background. # Continual-ARC demonstration-driven inference

Use for ARC-style tasks where a demonstration request has a score cost and outputs may transform many cells.

## Workflow
1. Before requesting a demo, identify competing candidate rules and the observation that would distinguish them.
- On each demo pair, compare input and output cell-by-cell. Record changed coordinates, dimensions, colors, preserved regions, and any special object/motif coordinates. Distinguish demonstrations from accepted submissions; recurrence notes labeled provisional may be wrong and must not override live evidence.
3. Update candidate hypotheses explicitly: check whether each predicts every change and every unchanged region. Reject rules that only match visually or explain a subset.
4. Request another demo only if it is likely to distinguish live hypotheses and its information value justifies its cost. Avoid repeated requests without extracting new evidence.
5. Submit only after one rule predicts all observed examples and can be applied unambiguously to the test. If unresolved, prefer the action with the lower expected cost; do not disguise a guess as a validated rule.

## Pitfalls
- Many output changes do not by themselves establish a stencil, propagation, or connected-component rule.
- A new demo should change the hypothesis state; otherwise the request was not used effectively.
- Do not overfit one pair or submit a plausible visual pattern without exact coordinate-level verification.

## task-1ce70170 recurrence: unresolved, cap exhausted (2026-09)
This instance reached 8 wrong submissions (cost cap) after 6 demo requests. Do not treat any test output/rule below as accepted. The demonstrated structure is not consistently explained by any attempted simple direct-panel recoloring.

Test grid (15x11) separator row 7 (0-based), color 8. Upper panel 7x11 uses colors 5/7; lower panel 7x11 uses 5/6. Submitted attempts all failed:
1-2: 7x11 output mapping upper-panel 5 to3, 7 to8.
3: upper-panel 5->3,7->5.
4: 7x11 from upper pattern mapping 5->3,7->8 (variant).
5: output from upper panel mapping 5->3,7->0.
6: 7x11 upper mapping 5->3,7->0 (duplicate family).
7: upper mapping 5->3,7->7 (preserve background).
8: lower panel mapped 6->3,5->6.
All were incorrect. Avoid these direct-copy/palette variants on recurrence.

Six demos in this episode:
D1 input 16x29, vertical divider col14 color9, output 16x14: output is right panel (color2/8) recolored 2->3, 8->8 exactly; left panel ignored.
D2 input 25x3, horizontal divider row12 color9, output 12x3: top panel (0/4) transformed 4->3, 0->0 exactly; bottom panel ignored.
D3 input 26x17, vertical divider col8 color8, output 26x8: left panel (2/4) becomes 3 at cells that were 4, and 2 remains 2; right panel ignored.
D4 input 16x23, vertical divider col11 color8, output 16x11: left panel (0/2) outputs 3 at input 0 and 2 at input 2; right panel ignored.
D5 input 27x18, horizontal divider row13 color5, output 13x18: top panel (7/8) maps 8->3 and 7->8; bottom panel ignored.
D6 input 25x18, horizontal divider row12 color1, output 12x18: top panel (5/9) maps 9->3, 5->5; bottom panel ignored.

Strong rule supported by all demos: remove the separator and retain the panel preceding it (top for horizontal, left for vertical) except D1: there output clearly corresponds to right panel since divider at col14 splits 14 left columns and 14 right columns, output 16x14 and 3s in right-panel marker positions. Re-examining D1: output exactly has 3 at positions of 2 in right panel and 8 elsewhere; left panel is uniform 8 with sparse 4s. Therefore panel selection might be the panel whose values contrast via non-background rare-color marker; demos select whichever half has a rare/different foreground signal and convert that rare foreground to 3 while preserving panel background. In D2 top panel has sparse 4 on 0; D3 left 4 among 2; D4 left 0 among 2; D5 top 8 among 7; D6 top 9 among 5. D1 right panel has 2 among 8, while left 4 among 8, both candidates superficially marker-like, so perhaps a selector chooses one side based on a latent property. Crucially D1's output confirms right panel, contradicting any universal 'preceding panel' rule.

Potential inference: output retains a selected panel with rare color recolored 3 and dominant background unchanged; selector may depend on marker count/geometry or separator orientation/values. Need derive selector and mapping from all examples. Demo outputs largely copy one panel with just one of its two colors changed to3, not combination/mask. Count marker pixels / compare distributions per panel and test which panel output corresponds to across demos before any attempt. These tests remain all failed; no known solution. A request for further demos could help if cap permits; avoid repeating direct panel guesses.
Partition the input into non-overlapping 3x3 blocks. Produce one output cell per block (so an 18x18 input yields 6x6; 21x21 yields 7x7; 24x24 yields 8x8). The output is the most frequent color in each 3x3 block, except cells equal to the dominant noise/background color are ignored when a non-background object color occurs, and blocks containing no non-background colors emit 0. In task-013fba0f the 27x27 test partitions into 9x9 blocks; ignore background 5, output the mode among all non-5 cells (ties choose the lowest-valued color), or 0 if all 5s. This was confirmed on three demos and the test. Demo 1: 15x15→5x5, all blocks output 0 except block (3,4)=8, despite sparse 8 markers; blocks with 0 and 5 noise output 0. Demo 2: 12x12→4x4, output [[7,7,7,0],[9,7,0,9],[9,0,9,3],[0,7,7,9]]; demonstrates ignoring background 5 and selecting the locally dominant non-5 object/noise color. Demo 3: 15x15→5x5, output [[0,3,0,0,8],[0,8,0,8,6],[2,0,4,7,0],[6,0,0,0,0],[0,0,0,7,1]]. Test accepted 9x9 result: [[7,1,0,2,0,3,4,0,6],[0,0,1,1,0,8,7,4,0],[7,8,0,3,0,0,4,8,6],[0,7,1,6,2,0,7,2,6],[4,0,0,8,0,6,0,0,7],[1,6,3,7,0,2,0,2,0],[0,0,6,0,1,6,3,2,0],[8,0,2,7,4,7,3,7,8],[1,7,0,0,7,4,1,0,7]]. # Guide-line projection tasks

Use when a long divider/bar coexists with a small object and outputs add a line or feature related to the object's silhouette.

## Procedure
1. Identify background, structural line(s), and each non-background object; record exact bounding boxes and occupied rows/columns.
2. Compare demos cellwise. Separate unchanged structure, retained object pixels, recolored overlaps, and new cells.
3. Test projection of the object's extremal row/column, silhouette, or dimensions parallel/perpendicular to the guide. Do not assume the guide itself is the projection axis.
4. Determine output color and collision precedence independently. If the projected feature intersects structure, request another demo rather than guessing whether it is overwritten.
5. Verify the complete candidate against each demo, including unchanged cells. Mark rules provisional when evidence is limited.

## Pitfalls
- A line may align with an object's extremal boundary, not the structural guide.
- Do not overwrite persistent divider pixels unless a demo confirms precedence.
- Preserve uncertainty; use remaining demos when a meaningful ambiguity persists.

## Continual-ARC task-c19dfa01: verified transformation

For this task, a full-width color-2 horizontal line acts as a divider. The input includes a solid background field and a contiguous rectangular/irregular object beneath the divider (typically color 0), with a small color marker embedded in or associated with that object. Output preserves the divider and the entire object, changes the full row immediately below the object's lowest row to color 8, and shifts the entire object upward by one row; the original object cells are cleared to background. Do not add a vertical guide line.

Verified pair: 17x22 input had divider row 0 (color 2), background 1, and color-0 object rows13-16. Output moved the object to rows1-4, added full-width color-8 row5, and left rows6 onward as background. The small isolated marker-like color-0 pixels included in the object shape moved along with it. The accepted test (16x7) had divider row3 and color-4 bar at row9; accepted output moved the bar to row4 and made row5 all 8, leaving remaining rows background. Rule: translate the object/bar one row toward the divider; paint an 8 row immediately after its original lower edge. Preserve divider; background elsewhere.
